status: adopted for Phase F specification; not complete-plan or runtime acceptance
title: Common authority for admitted work and surviving obligations
problem: Cross-domain work must have continuing custody and a consistent agenda without making the owner the routine coordinator.
decision: Adopt S1.0, derived from repaired A, with one logical admission authority, native production and protected consequence/evidence/recovery boundaries.
alternatives: S0 native tools with manual coordination
B native federation and independent issuers
epistemic_basis: Structural inference: fewer independently administered internal coordination contracts; no measured superiority.
reversibility: Repository-local specification remains reversible; operational promises, disclosure and lost data require separate consequence decisions.
reopen_trigger: Reopen if omitted duties or proportional owner coordination persist; prefer S0 if equivalent outcomes cost less, B for beneficial real administrative autonomy, C2 for useful neglected inquiry.

title: Specialized production without a department-agent roster
problem: Actual company delivery needs different methods and competent standing, not a named model per function.
decision: Allocate known predicates to deterministic code, waits/repetition to durable procedures, interpretation/generation to bounded model work, and real human/professional/physical work to accepted capable performers.
epistemic_basis: Design allocation by work/authority; persistent identity benefit remains unproved.
accepted_design_costs: Unavailable real performers remain operational blockers
reversibility: Repository-local specification remains reversible; operational promises, disclosure and lost data require separate consequence decisions.
reopen_trigger: Reopen an allocation when measured outcomes, cost or continuity favor another mode without greater unauthorized consequence.

status: adopted for Phase F specification; not complete-plan or runtime acceptance
title: Bounded string ceiling for the canonical value schema
problem: values.schema.json#/$defs/string was an unconstrained {"type": "string"} resolved by 907 references, so every bounded field in the contract registries inherited no bound at all. An unbounded string in a canonically hashed, durably stored record is a storage and denial-of-service surface, and the schema could not refuse a payload no implementation would want to keep.
decision: Set maxLength 8192 characters and forbid C0 and C7 control characters except tab, newline and carriage return. The ceiling is a mechanism decision taken to replace an absent bound, not a value derived from any observed field length; it is revisable through an explicit schema migration under the kernel's evolution rules.
alternatives: Leave the type unconstrained, which is the pre-repair state and constrains 907 references to nothing
Set per-field ceilings at each of the 907 reference sites, which is more precise and 907 places to drift
Set a higher or lower shared ceiling, which is the same decision at a different number
epistemic_basis: Design decision under an absent bound. No field-length distribution was measured and none is claimed: the schema's own description says the exact ceiling is a storage and denial-of-service decision and is flagged for the founder, not derived.
accepted_design_costs: A field that legitimately needs more than 8192 characters must be a blob reference or a schema migration, not a longer string
The ceiling is shared, so it is simultaneously too large for short identifiers and too small for long documents; per-field precision is traded for one place to change
reversibility: Repository-local specification remains reversible; operational promises, disclosure and lost data require separate consequence decisions.
reopen_trigger: Reopen if an admitted record type genuinely requires a longer inline value, if a measured field-length distribution contradicts the ceiling, or if the founder sets a different storage bound. Changing it is a schema major change and requires the migration protocol of 01 section 11, not a field rename. Origin: canonical repair R6.

status: adopted for Phase F specification; not complete-plan or runtime acceptance
title: Per-phase criterion content is authored by derivation from the prose contracts, never invented
problem: FI-11's mechanism is closed — every edge guard calls its own criterion_id and declared-but-unread arguments are gone — but the CONTENT is not: for 167 of 173 records the source corpus states no per-phase evidence requirement, so two criteria of one record can still differ only by the criterion a judgment must name. The tempting repair is to write plausible per-phase requirements, which would put invented obligations into an executable registry and make the guard distinctness metric go green on fiction.
decision: Author the missing per-phase criterion content by derivation from the prose contracts, with a citation to the passage each requirement comes from. Where the prose is silent on a phase, mark that criterion content_unspecified and register the gap rather than filling it. A criterion with no cited source is not admitted.
alternatives: Invent plausible per-phase requirements, which greens guard_distinctness.py on content nothing supports
Leave all 167 as they are, which keeps 1295 edges sharing one meaning tail and leaves FI-11's defect reproduced at edge scale
Delete the per-phase criterion mechanism, which would discard a repair that is already correct
epistemic_basis: Design decision about how to close a content gap, not a measurement. The 167-of-173 figure and the one-shared-meaning-tail finding are F-canonical-01's; re-measure with contracts/tools/guard_distinctness.py rather than quoting them.
accepted_design_costs: Derivation is slower than authoring and will leave content_unspecified criteria standing where the prose genuinely says nothing, so the distinctness metric will not reach a clean number
Each registered gap is a specification obligation someone must later discharge, and the register will carry them visibly rather than absorbing them
reversibility: Repository-local specification remains reversible; operational promises, disclosure and lost data require separate consequence decisions.
reopen_trigger: Reopen if a prose contract is amended to state a per-phase requirement that an existing criterion contradicts, or if the count of content_unspecified criteria stops falling across specification revisions. Origin: F-canonical-01, FI-11 content residue; the lane docs/vision-phase-content is in flight.

status: adopted; mechanism decision derived from the selected architecture; revisable by a reviewed ChangeProposal
owner: orchestrator (decision); canonical contract author (implementation); independent reviewer (recheck)
title: Performance of a sale is accepted delivery plus discharged or transferred obligations — never payment alone
problem: G2-01 (d): criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1 demanded exactly what accepted demanded; SalesAgreement had no relation to Fulfillment; a paid but undelivered sale could reach performed. "What evidence constitutes performance of a sale" was unstated, and the two available inventions (payment settled / delivery accepted) describe different companies.
decision: SalesAgreement gains /payload/fulfillment_ref → Fulfillment; criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1 requires Fulfillment in a delivered/accepted state and every linked Obligation discharged or transferred; payment settlement moves the agreement to accepted or partially-performed, not performed. Fulfillment gains a domain lifecycle (proposed → delivering → delivered → failed | refunded) with an authenticated attributable event on the delivered edge.
alternatives: Payment settled = performed (rejected: makes a paid-but-undelivered sale complete; contradicts SalesAgreement.invariants[0] and 02 §6)
Leave to implementation (rejected: the reviewer showed this is the silent path, and both choices are plausible to an implementer)

Split into performed_paid and performed_delivered (rejected: two "performed" states invite the same conflation the protocol names; the existing accepted / partially-performed states already hold the paid-not-delivered case)
evidence_and_reasoning: 02 §3 "accepted work cannot discharge external standing through an internal status"; 02 §6 "Delivery produces independently observed results"; the record's own invariant "performance is shown by substantive fulfillment" was enforced by nothing (G2-01 counterexample validated). Requiring Fulfillment delivered and Obligations discharged/transferred makes the prose true.
epistemic_basis: Decision. Derived from the adopted S1.0 selection (02-architecture-selection.md §3, §6) and from the consistency of the existing closure-edge set in contracts/record-registry.json; not from new evidence and not from a founder value. The Phase G reviewer classified the gap (d): implementation would otherwise settle it silently.
accepted_design_costs: Fulfillment must gain a domain lifecycle (G2-05) before any sale can reach performed; a service with no observable delivery event cannot be marked performed by payment alone and must record why. More edges, more evidence, less convenience — deliberately.
external_exposure_authorized: None. A contract change; no spend, publication, contact or deployment.
reversibility: Reversible before B04 by editing the SalesAgreement/Fulfillment contracts; after live sales, a migration under 02 §10 (T-R1).
reopen_trigger: A lawful offer class whose performance genuinely IS payment (e.g. a donation with no deliverable) that the Fulfillment lifecycle cannot represent without a fictitious delivery; or measured owner labor from performing the distinction exceeding its benefit under CF1 maintenance comparison.
implementation_evidence: None yet. Guard repair lane owed; independent recheck owed; no runtime exists.

status: adopted; mechanism decision derived from the selected architecture; revisable by a reviewed ChangeProposal
owner: orchestrator (decision); canonical contract author (implementation); independent reviewer (recheck)
title: Terminating a sales agreement is a closure event; surviving duties live in terminated_with_residuals
problem: G2-02 (d): the four SalesAgreement:*→terminated edges carried transition_basis only, while every other closure edge in the registry carries due_preserved; there was no terminated_with_residuals state, so terminating a disputed sale with recognized obligations succeeded and asserted closure with nothing having looked.
decision: All four SalesAgreement:*→terminated edges carry due_preserved; a new terminal state terminated_with_residuals holds the case where the transitive due set is not empty, with an accepted custodian for each residual, matching Commitment:made→ended_with_residuals and CAP-39 closed-with-residuals. terminated asserts that nothing is owed.
alternatives: Declare termination not a closure event (rejected: would have to explain why Commitment ended, Offer withdrawn and Case abandoned — the same act at another record — all carry due_preserved)

due_preserved without a residuals state (rejected: forces either refusal to terminate while duties survive, or silent closure; the Commitment and CAP-39 precedent is a residuals state with custodians)
evidence_and_reasoning: Consistency of the existing closure-edge set (Commitment, Offer, Case, GrievanceCase, Obligation, Fulfillment, ClosurePlan, Venture); 02 §3 "an obligation survives that case"; protocol §Changeability "old effects or duties cannot disappear". The reviewer's counterexample (three recognized obligations and an open SupportCase survive a successful terminate) validated at 7ddc066.
epistemic_basis: Decision. Derived from the adopted S1.0 selection (02-architecture-selection.md §3, §6) and from the consistency of the existing closure-edge set in contracts/record-registry.json; not from new evidence and not from a founder value. The Phase G reviewer classified the gap (d): implementation would otherwise settle it silently.
accepted_design_costs: Terminating a sale now requires computing the transitive due set at the witnessed frontier and assigning a custodian to each residual; a terminate that cannot do so lands in terminated_with_residuals rather than terminated.
external_exposure_authorized: None. A contract change; no spend, publication, contact or deployment.
reversibility: Reversible before B04 by editing the SalesAgreement/Fulfillment contracts; after live sales, a migration under 02 §10 (T-R1).
reopen_trigger: A demonstrated class of sale whose termination can never carry residuals (would make the state dead weight); or due_preserved cost at termination measurably dominating ordinary closure work.
implementation_evidence: None yet. Guard repair lane owed; independent recheck owed; no runtime exists.
